fields.label: Headline
fields.value: Free music lessons for kids, taught by high school musicians

fields.label: Sub-headline
fields.value: Meaning in Music pairs children across the Bay Area with experienced high school instructors for weekly one-on-one lessons. Lessons are always free, and we loan instruments to families who need one.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Making music education accessible to every child

fields.label: Paragraph 1
fields.value: Private music lessons in our area typically cost $50 to $80 an hour, and some local elementary schools have no music program at all. For many families, that puts learning an instrument out of reach.

fields.label: Paragraph 2
fields.value: Meaning in Music was founded in 2022 by students at The Athenian School to help close that gap. Our volunteer instructors are high school musicians with years of training who teach younger students one-on-one, every week, at no cost to families.

fields.label: Headline
fields.value: Music lessons for every child, not just those who can afford them

fields.label: Sub-headline
fields.value: Meaning in Music is a student-run nonprofit founded at The Athenian School in Danville, California. High school musicians teach free, one-on-one lessons to younger students across the Bay Area, and we loan instruments to families who need them.

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Any kid who wants to learn music should get to, whatever their family can afford. We do that with free lessons from high school instructors, a lending library of donated instruments, and fundraising for school music programs that need help.

fields.label: Paragraph 1
fields.value: Those of us who grew up playing had a few things in common: a parent who could pay for lessons, an instrument at home, and usually a school orchestra or band to join. Plenty of kids a few miles away had none of those. Lessons around here run $50 to $80 an hour, a starter instrument costs a few hundred dollars, and at least one district near us has no elementary music program at all.

fields.label: Paragraph 2
fields.value: So in the fall of 2022 we started doing what we were actually able to do. We asked classmates who wanted to teach. We wrote a letter to our neighbors asking for instruments that were sitting unused in closets and garages. We posted on elementary school Facebook pages. Our first calls with families happened that October.

fields.label: Story p3
fields.value: Those calls were the best part. A parent would tell us their daughter had taught herself to read music, or that their son's school didn't have a music class to join. Then we'd talk to the kid, who usually had a song in mind already.

fields.label: Photo credit
fields.value: The Meaning in Music group after a concert, 2026.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: What a weekly lesson actually does

fields.label: Why p1
fields.value: Learning to read notes matters, and so does practicing scales. But we think the most important part of a lesson is simpler than that: an older kid shows up every week, knows your name, remembers the song you were stuck on, and is genuinely happy when you get it.

fields.label: Why p2
fields.value: That's what a lot of us had growing up, and it's the reason we kept playing. It's also why every kid gets their own teacher instead of a spot in a group class.

fields.label: For families — text
fields.value: It costs nothing. You fill out a form, we have a short call with you and your kid, and we match them with a teacher. If they need an instrument to start, we lend one.

fields.label: For children — text
fields.value: Thirty minutes a week with a teacher who plays your instrument and wants to hear what you've been practicing. You pick the songs as much as we do.

fields.label: For high schoolers — text
fields.value: You get a real student from your first week. We help you plan lessons, and you'll find out quickly that explaining something is harder than playing it.

fields.label: For schools & partners — text
fields.value: We can come play for your students, help spread the word about lessons, and send donated instruments to music programs that need them.

fields.label: Paragraph 1
fields.value: Nobody at Meaning in Music is paid. The teachers, the organizers, and the person who built this website are all high school students. What we raise goes to instruments and repairs, lesson books and sheet music, and school music programs that need help.

fields.label: Paragraph 2
fields.value: We're working toward 501(c)(3) status so we can apply for more grants and reach more kids. A donated guitar, a few dollars from a bake sale, and a grant all end up the same way: as lessons.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: What we try to stick to

fields.label: Value 1 — description
fields.value: We started this because we love music. We want kids to love it too, not just get through it.

fields.label: Value 2 — description
fields.value: Lessons happen every week and instruments get delivered. We'd rather do small things reliably than big things once.

fields.label: Value 3 — description
fields.value: We track lessons taught, kids taught, and hours played, because that's how we know whether this is working.

fields.label: Value 4 — description
fields.value: Classical, pop, whatever a kid wants to play. Music belongs to every kid, whatever their background.

fields.label: Value 5 — description
fields.value: Kids keep playing when someone they look up to is in their corner. The relationship is the point.

fields.label: Paragraph 1
fields.value: Meaning in Music began at The Athenian School, a school in Danville at the foot of Mount Diablo that puts a lot of weight on service and leadership.

fields.label: Paragraph 2
fields.value: We know we've been lucky. Most of us have had good teachers, good instruments, and parents who drove us to rehearsals. This is our way of passing some of that along to kids who live a few miles away and haven't had the same luck.

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Sign up a kid for lessons, teach with us, give an instrument, or just tell a family who might want this. Any of those helps.

fields.label: Headline
fields.value: The people who show up every week

fields.label: Sub-headline
fields.value: Meaning in Music is run entirely by students. These are the three of us who started it and keep it organized, and below them, the instructors who do the teaching.

fields.label: Luca — bio
fields.value: Luca has played piano for twelve years and spends a lot of his free time writing music. He studies composition and music theory at the San Francisco Conservatory, and co-directs Meaning in Music with Lilian.

fields.label: Lilian — bio
fields.value: Lilian has played piano for twelve years. She co-directs Meaning in Music and leads our outreach, which is how most families hear about us in the first place.

fields.label: Henry — bio
fields.value: Henry has played piano for eleven years and violin for six. He handles logistics: the budget, this website, and the day-to-day work of getting instruments and schedules where they need to be.
